full_judgment: 7. We have heard Mr. N.K. Saha, the learned Senior Advocate appearing for the petitioner, and Mr. Nawab Ali, the learned Advocate-On-Record appearing for the respondent No.1 and perused the impugned judgment of this Division and also perused the other judgments in question and also other materials available on record. It appears that in the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal this Division considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner to the effect that- the trial court decreed the suit holding that the plaintiff claimed his title on the basis of deed of settlement dated 28.05.1948 which was registered prior to the registered kabuliyat dated 07.06.1948 produced by the defendant and further the title of the plaintiff has already been declared in Title Suit No. 265 of 1976 and though the defendant claimed the Title Suit No. 295 of 1996 challenging the decree passed in the Title Suit No. 265 of 1976 yet he did not get any relief therein and further the evidence on record also show that the plaintiff was given possession in kha schedule land but thereafter the plaintiff was dispossessed from a portion thereof.
